topics.title: Once you understand inflation, you'll never keep your savings in cash again

demand.title: Why can't prices just stay the same? (Vox)

topics.angle: Your $10,000 in a drawer still says $10,000 in 20 years. It just buys what $5,537 buys today.
topics.why_now: Everyone everywhere feels prices rising: 'Why everything feels more expensive now' 5.4M, Vox 2.5M and 1.4M, How Money Works 'How Is Everything Outpacing Inflation At The Same Time?' 1.55M (6 months old). Global, universal mechanics, and our maths covers it end to end (real_return, price_rise). No long video of ours has told inflation.

promise (by 0:20): six things inflation does to your money that nobody says out loud, and the last one is the reason the rich are never in cash
item 1, the drawer: $10,000 at an assumed 3% inflation buys what $5,537 buys today after 20 years (real_return, rate 0) — the bill shrinks, reveal by 0:45
item 2, the bank account: at 4% it reads $21,911 but buys $12,132 of today's goods: a real 1% a year (real_return) — Priya's chart: the number line climbing while the buying-power line barely moves
recap-and-tease at ~2:30: 'so a bank barely keeps up. Now watch what it does to your bills'
item 3, the rent: $1,500 a month at 3% is $2,709 in 20 years, $138,177 extra paid along the way (price_rise) — second reveal at ~2:00-3:00
item 4, the raise that isn't: $60,000 rising 2% a year is $73,140 in 10 years, but worth $54,423 of today's money: a pay cut (real_return) — Sharma has seen it before
recap-and-tease at ~5:00: 'so who wins when prices rise?'
item 5, the groceries: $600 a month at 4% is $888 in 10 years (price_rise) — Rohan's cart scene

item 6 (strongest, ~2/3 in): the same $10,000 owned instead of saved, at an assumed 7%, is $38,697, $21,426 in today's money (real_return): the rich hold things that rise with prices — the one chart with three lines (cash, bank, owned), cash going neutral grey
payoff: inflation is a tax on cash; the one rule: money you won't need for years shouldn't sit still
ending within 30 s: one CTA, disclaimer end card
